notes.1a: (i) Few candidates identified water as the solvent in milk. Calcium and lactose were the most common incorrect responses.
notes.1aii: Few candidates completed Table 1.1 correctly. Many did not identify the enzyme appropriate for each nutrient. The products of protein digestion were well-known, but often glycerol was omitted for the products of fat digestion. The correct elements present in each nutrient were given by only a small proportion of candidates. A common error was the omission of nitrogen in protein.
notes.1b: (i) Some candidates identified the importance of vitamin D in the development of strong bones and in preventing rickets, but fewer mentioned its role in the development of teeth. Some vague descriptions of growth were also seen but could not be credited.
notes.1bii: Some candidates described the importance of iron in the diet although many simply described the symptoms of anaemia. Often candidates did not make it clear that iron is needed for making the haemoglobin in red blood cells. Many simply stated that iron was needed for making blood.
notes.1c: (i) Most candidates defined the term transmissible disease by referring to the disease passing from one person to another; however, far fewer stated that this type of disease is caused by a pathogen.
notes.1cii: Only a few candidates stated that rubella was caused by a virus. Few candidates explained that the virus that causes rubella can cross the placenta and affect the fetus. Some vague responses were 0610 Biology June 2021 seen where it was not clear that rubella was affecting the fetus during pregnancy. Very few candidates described the immunity gained through vaccination in sufficient detail to gain credit.
notes.1iii: Many candidates identified a lack of protein as a cause of kwashiorkor, but very few went further by referring to the inadequate diet that a child receives when weaned. Many described the physical effects of the disease instead and gained no credit.
notes.2a: (i) Some candidates correctly named molecule A in Fig. 2.1 as mRNA. Many alternative answers were seen including gene, which is not a molecule and so not creditworthy.
notes.2aii: Some candidates identified structure B as a ribosome, but as with 2(a)(i) a wide range of incorrect responses were seen, including protein and pancreas.
notes.2iii: Candidates were required to explain that molecule A (mRNA) is a copy of the gene for insulin that moves from the nucleus to a ribosome in the cytoplasm. Candidates were also expected to state that as mRNA moves through the ribosome its sequence of bases determines the order in which amino acids are assembled to make the protein.
notes.2b: Only a few candidates stated that insulin is a hormone. Many explained that insulin balances out, levels or regulates blood sugar. None of these answers were accepted as insulin’s role is to decrease the concentration of glucose in the blood. Some candidates stated that insulin has its effect by stimulating the storage of glucose as glycogen; however, very few explained this in sufficient detail to gain marks. Some candidates stated that insulin reduces the concentration of glucose in the body.
notes.2c: Few candidates named two substances secreted by the pancreas. The most common incorrect answers were bile, glucose and amino acids. There was confusion between glucagon and glycogen.
notes.3a: (i) Some candidates answered this question well linking the effect of temperature on enzymes correctly to the rate of photosynthesis. Other candidates were confused as to why temperature has an effect on the rate of photosynthesis. Many linked their answer to transpiration rate rather than to the effect of temperature on enzymes. Few candidates mentioned an increase in the kinetic energy of the molecules. Some said that there would be an increase in effective collisions, but they did not state they were between enzyme and substrate molecules.
notes.3aii: Most candidates could not explain the effect of low humidity on photosynthesis, incorrectly stating that the low amount of water in the air meant that photosynthesis did not have enough water as a reactant.
notes.3iii: Most candidates explained why the results in Table 3.1 were expressed as per cm2 rather than per leaf.
notes.3b: (i) Nearly all candidates read the correct figures from the graph.
notes.3bii: Very few candidates realised that the rate at which carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis is greater than the rate of carbon dioxide uptake because plant cells produce carbon dioxide in respiration. Some explained that changes in temperature were responsible. Others referred to the presence of stored carbon dioxide in the leaf.
notes.3c: There were many good attempts at this question on the growth of crops in glasshouses. Many candidates discussed the idea of using heaters or methods of cooling, but few explained that it is necessary to maintain optimum temperatures. Carbon dioxide was seen as an important factor to control, but very few suggested that carbon dioxide enrichment is used. Few stated that extra carbon dioxide can be provided by burning fuels or from tanks of compressed carbon dioxide. Light 0610 Biology June 2021 was also seen as an important factor to control, but many discussed this in the terms of sunlight instead of light intensity and suggested that it could be improved by using natural lighting instead of identifying artificial light as a key component. Many candidates correctly mentioned the idea of increasing yield and protection from extreme weather conditions so that production became continuous or independent of seasons. Many candidates described the protection of plants from damage by pests.
notes.4a: Most candidates described hunting or poaching as a threat to large mammals, such as rhinos, and the threat posed by humans causing habitat destruction. Fewer candidates then explained why humans needed the land. A lack of sufficient food and the effects of climate change were often correctly given.
notes.4b: (i) Only a few candidates stated that the brother-sister mating described in the question was inbreeding. However, many identified that this would lead to reduced variation with the consequences of an increased chance of genetic disease and birth defects. Candidates often stated that this breeding programme would increase the number of mutations that would occur. However, it is correct to say that it is likely to increase the expression of any mutations in the offspring of a brother-sister mating because this leads to an increase in homozygosity.
notes.4bii: The process of artificial insemination (AI) was not described in sufficient detail by most candidates. Many candidates stated that sperm is collected, but then went on to describe in vitro fertilisation (IVF) rather than artificial insemination. A few candidates suggested the need for screening of the sperm before use in AI.
notes.5a: Most candidates named the diaphragm in row 1 of Table 5.1 and alveoli in row 4. Candidates often did not state which set of intercostal muscles (external or internal) were involved in decreasing air pressure in the lungs and in forced expiration and so did not gain credit for their answers in rows 1 and 3.
notes.5b: Many candidates described the overall trend in Fig. 5.1, but few gave correct data quotes. Many candidates did not give units with their data quotes. The most common points made were that the rate and depth of breathing increased with increased carbon dioxide concentration and then decreased as the concentration decreased. Few recognised that there was a larger increase in the rate of breathing than the depth of breathing.
notes.5c: Most candidates completed the second paragraph correctly, but fewer completed the first paragraph with respiration and mitochondria.
notes.6a: Some candidates completed the genetic diagram correctly, but fewer wrote out the correct phenotypes. Some candidates did not use the alleles for the blood group gene correctly despite them being given in the question stem. Many candidates gave the correct probability that the child will have blood group O.
notes.6b: Many candidates gave the AB blood group as an example of co-dominance, but fewer could explain what this meant. Many discussed genes or genotypes instead of alleles or failed to state that they are expressed in the phenotype.
notes.6c: Some candidates used Fig. 6.1 to explain discontinuous variation as having limited categories; fewer went on to explain the role of genes and the environment in discontinuous variation. Many described the data in the bar chart rather than answering the question.
